anjali: Canary hit a nondeterministic stale-residency during concurrent snapshot+compact. Repro steps: start 3 tenants, hot prefixes, force compaction at 80% slab, trigger snapshot same slab. Fail ~1/30.

anjali: Paste of key log lines: ```
[2026-03-23T11:12:01Z] snapshot commit slab=27 epoch=2010 residency=HOT
[2026-03-23T11:12:01Z] compaction apply slab=27 tombstones reap -> residency=STALE
```

peter: Sounds like a visibility/order problem. Do we have any in-memory fence between snapshot commit and residency flip?

kai: We don't. Our commit currently publishes epoch then updates residency flag; compaction can apply concurrently and win.

anjali: Proposal: emit tiny handshake events for snapshot_commit and compaction_finish (single-line JSON in traces), and add a canary-only flag compaction_quiesce_on_snapshot=true to force ordering during repro.

kai: Also add a metric handshake_misorders_total and a debug-only assert that fails if compaction finalizes while snapshot commit is 'in-flight' for same slab.

infra-bot: Canary started kv-canary-2026-03-23 run=1 at 6624000005.

peter: For long-term, consider atomicizing residency flip into snapshot commit (one code path) so compaction can't race. That is trickier but cleaner. File an RFC follow-up.

anjali: I'll open a tiny PR for traces + canary flag. Owners: tracing=kai, canary=peter, tests=anjali. I'll run 100 iterations with quiesce=true and post traces if repros appear.

infra-bot: Canary progress: 40/100 at 6624000020.

anjali: Thanks — will report back.
